title: Choose the right storage type
description: Choose storage from measured latency, IOPS, throughput, durability, protocol, access mode, and cost requirements. Azure Disk normally provides single-node read/write access; Azure Files provides shared file access. Validate filesystem semantics and driver/OS support, especially for Blob CSI mounts, rather than treating object storage as a fully POSIX-compatible filesystem.

documentation.title: Storage considerations for Azure Kubernetes Service

title: Size the nodes for storage needs
description: Size nodes for disk attachment limits, aggregate IOPS and throughput, network bandwidth, and local ephemeral capacity as well as CPU and memory. Include failover, scale-out, and upgrade surge demands; a disk's advertised performance can be constrained by the VM or storage account.
detail: Different types and sizes of nodes are available. Each node (underlying VM) size provides a different amount of core resources such as CPU and memory. These VM sizes have a maximum number of disks that can be attached. Storage performance also varies between VM sizes for the maximum local and attached disk IOPS (input/output operations per second). If your applications require Azure Disks as their storage solution, plan for and choose an appropriate node VM size. The amount of CPU and memory isn't the only factor when you choose a VM size. The storage capabilities are also important.

documentation.title: Size the nodes for storage needs

title: Dynamically provision volumes
description: Prefer dynamic provisioning through explicit CSI StorageClasses and PVCs, while retaining static provisioning for existing volumes or controlled recovery when appropriate. Set reclaimPolicy deliberately: Delete can remove underlying storage after PVC deletion, whereas Retain requires manual lifecycle management. Deleting a pod alone does not normally delete its PVC or volume.

title: Secure and back up your data
description: Encrypt data at rest and in transit where supported, restrict storage access, and use Azure Backup for AKS or another supported solution appropriate to each volume type. Azure Site Recovery is not an AKS cluster backup mechanism. Monitor backup failures and test restores of data and required Kubernetes resources.
detail: Snapshots are generally crash-consistent, not automatically application-consistent or atomic across volumes. Use supported application hooks or database-native backup and recovery to meet consistency needs. Inventory skipped or unsupported volumes, protect external data services separately, and do not install the AKS Backup extension alongside Velero.

documentation.title: Secure and back up your data

title: Evaluate managed data services for durable application state
description: Where appropriate, use managed data services such as Azure SQL, Azure Storage, or Azure Cosmos DB instead of operating stateful infrastructure in AKS. Evaluate consistency, latency, connectivity, cost, data residency, backup, and regional failover requirements before choosing.
detail: Externalizing state reduces cluster recovery coupling but does not automatically configure replication or protect against deletion and corruption. Set and test each service's backup and failover policies. Stateful workloads can also run on AKS when their storage and operational requirements are explicitly managed.

documentation.title: AKS microservices architecture and external data services

title: Evaluate and select a suitable node OS disk type
applicability: Node pools where the VM SKU supports ephemeral OS disks and local placement, capacity, and lifecycle requirements are compatible; managed OS disks remain valid when they better meet requirements.
description: Compare supported ephemeral and managed OS disks against measured OS, container image, log, and local workload capacity, I/O, provisioning-time, and cost requirements. Ephemeral OS disks can reduce OS disk latency and node provisioning time, but their contents are not durable. Record the selected disk type and test evidence instead of requiring every pool to use ephemeral disks.
detail: Verify SKU placement and capacity requirements and explicitly plan OS disk sizing at node-pool creation. Check compatibility with planned stop/start and scale-down behavior before choosing a disk type. Keep durable application data on suitable persistent storage or managed services; node replacement, reimage, or failure can lose local contents.

title: Evaluate Ultra Disk or Premium SSD v2 for demanding storage workloads
applicability: Only workloads whose measured storage performance requirements justify evaluating Ultra Disk or Premium SSD v2 on supported VM sizes and regions.
description: Benchmark Ultra Disk and Premium SSD v2 when standard disk tiers cannot meet latency, IOPS, or throughput requirements. Record achieved performance and total cost under representative load; retaining another supported tier is a valid outcome. Validate AKS CSI, VM size, region/zone, caching, encryption, and backup compatibility before selecting a tier.
detail: Provision only justified performance and verify both disk and VM limits. These disk types have availability and configuration restrictions; do not assume ZRS support or that snapshot, restore, and performance changes complete instantly.

documentation.title: Use Azure ultra disks on AKS

title: Keep durable data off container writable layers and node-local storage
description: Persist data that must survive container, pod, or node replacement on suitable persistent volumes or external services. Treat writable container layers, emptyDir, hostPath, and local NVMe storage as disposable unless application-level replication and recovery explicitly cover their loss.
detail: emptyDir survives a container restart within a pod but is deleted with the pod. A PersistentVolume object alone does not establish durability: local volumes remain tied to a node. Define recovery behavior for caches, checkpoints, and write-ahead logs and test abrupt node loss.

title: Align disk redundancy, volume binding, and pod topology
description: For zonal LRS disks, use WaitForFirstConsumer so provisioning respects pod scheduling topology and ensure sufficient nodes can run the pod in the disk's zone. Consider supported ZRS disk SKUs when cross-zone attachment is required. Validate the actual StorageClass and region capabilities rather than assuming defaults; ZRS does not provide simultaneous multi-node writes or automatic application failover.

documentation.title: Azure Disk CSI topology and ZRS support

title: Size node OS disks and bound local ephemeral-storage consumption
description: Size node OS disks from measured image cache, writable layers, logs, pod density, and I/O needs rather than assuming a larger disk alone fixes performance. Set container ephemeral-storage requests and limits, bound emptyDir volumes, configure supported log rotation, and alert on disk pressure and inode exhaustion. OS disk size changes require a replacement node pool.

documentation.title: Default OS disk sizing in AKS

title: Use supported CSI drivers and migrate legacy in-tree volumes
description: Use supported AKS CSI drivers for Azure Disk, Files, or Blob storage. Inventory legacy in-tree StorageClasses and PVs and follow the documented migration process, including backups and restore tests. Automatic CSI migration does not make an in-tree PV definition eligible for Azure Backup for AKS; verify explicit CSI volume definitions and supported snapshot configuration.

documentation.title: Use CSI storage drivers on AKS

title: Test volume expansion, retention, and recovery lifecycle
description: Alert on persistent-volume capacity and performance, enable allowVolumeExpansion where supported, and test the driver's filesystem expansion and restart requirements. Do not assume volumes can shrink. Review PVC, PV, snapshot, and StorageClass retention together, and test restore and reattachment without deleting the only durable copy.
